document_metadata.title: 1、EXT. TITLE SEQUENCE P
document_metadata.summary: Amid religious conflict, Protestant England, led by Elizabeth, resists Catholic Spain's Philip, who seeks to restore Catholicism in Europe by divine mandate.

entities.description: England, depicted as a weak and impoverished nation ruled by a woman, stands as the sole obstacle to Philip's ambitions of religious and territorial control.

document_metadata.summary: Raleigh presents gold taken from a Spanish ship to Elizabeth, who acknowledges it as piracy; he defends it as protecting England, earns her approval, and is welcomed home despite her teasing about his attire.

entities.description: Don Guerau, the Spanish Ambassador, identifies Raleigh as a pirate and claims the contents of the hampers are stolen Spanish treasure, confronting Queen Elizabeth.

entities.description: Raleigh informs Elizabeth that he has claimed a fertile coast in the New World in her name and named it Virginia to honor her status as the Virgin Queen.

entities.description: Noticing the presence of Wanchese and Manteo, Elizabeth asks Raleigh who the native Americans are and whether they have their own ruler.

entities.name: Manteo shakes Elizabeth's hand instead of kissing it
entities.description: Unfamiliar with court etiquette, Manteo misinterprets the Queen's gesture and shakes her hand rather than kissing it, causing shock among the courtiers.

entities.name: Elizabeth accepts Manteo's handshake and welcomes the native Americans
entities.description: Rather than taking offense, Elizabeth gracefully accepts the unconventional gesture and declares the native Americans welcome at court.

entities.name: Calley leads Wanchese and Manteo away from the court
entities.description: To prevent further cultural misunderstandings, Calley quickly ushers the native Americans out of the royal presence after their audience with the Queen.

entities.description: Raleigh offers symbolic gifts from the New World—mud and leaves—to Queen Elizabeth, which amuses her and elicits suppressed laughter from the court.

entities.description: Don Guerau interrupts the gift-giving by reiterating his claim that the items Raleigh presents are illicit spoils taken from Spanish ships.

entities.description: Elizabeth inspects the unusual offerings brought by Raleigh, reacting with humor to the presentation of mud and leaves from the New World.

document_metadata.title: 29、INT. GREAT HALL, WHITEHALL PALACE - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth confides in Walsingham, calling the Archduke a sweet boy and expressing concern she does not want him harmed by Walsingham's schemes, adding tension beneath courtly decorum.

entities.name: Archduke Charles delivers a formal love speech to Queen Elizabeth
entities.description: The sixteen-year-old Archduke Charles, trembling with shyness, recites a rehearsed speech praising Queen Elizabeth's beauty, wisdom, and divine presence, declaring himself conquered by her and dependent on her love for life.

entities.name: Austrian Ambassador prompts Archduke Charles during his speech
entities.description: As Archduke Charles struggles through his formal address, the Austrian Ambassador stands nearby, silently mouthing the words to help him remember his lines.

entities.name: Courtiers react with amusement and Spaniards sneer at Archduke's speech
entities.description: While the courtiers exchange knowing smiles at the Archduke's awkward performance, the Spanish delegation openly mocks the display, revealing political tensions beneath the ceremonial surface.

entities.name: Queen Elizabeth responds with dignified formality to Archduke's declaration
entities.description: Elizabeth acknowledges the Archduke's elaborate speech with graceful composure, thanking him for the honor and suggesting dinner may be as restorative as her love, maintaining ceremonial decorum.

entities.name: Raleigh and Calley enter the Great Hall during the royal dinner
entities.description: Raleigh arrives at the banquet with Calley following behind, joining the onlookers as the royal meal commences, marking his presence at court in formal attire.

entities.name: Raleigh engages in flirtatious conversation with court ladies
entities.description: Dressed in court fashion and drawing admiring glances, Raleigh exchanges witty remarks about naval combat with a court lady and shares a meaningful smile with Bess, indicating romantic interest.

entities.description: A court jester moves among the guests, entertaining them with comedic antics and pranks as part of the spectacle surrounding the royal meal.

entities.name: Queen Elizabeth notices Raleigh flirting with court ladies
entities.description: While seated beside Archduke Charles, Elizabeth glances toward Raleigh and observes him engaging flirtatiously with the female courtiers, registering his behavior amidst the diplomatic proceedings.

document_metadata.title: 29、INT. GREAT HALL, WHITEHALL PALACE - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth confides in Walsingham, calling the Archduke a sweet boy and expressing concern she does not want him harmed by Walsingham's schemes, adding tension beneath courtly decorum.

entities.name: Elizabeth shares her technique for coping with public dining
entities.description: Elizabeth notices the young Archduke's discomfort at the dinner table and confides in Bess, explaining that she pretends there is an imaginary pane of glass between herself and others to manage the pressure of eating in public.

entities.name: Elizabeth notices Bess staring at Raleigh
entities.description: Elizabeth observes Bess gazing intently at Raleigh, follows her line of sight, and becomes amused upon realizing that Bess is also focused on Raleigh, who is flirting with court ladies.

entities.name: Elizabeth instructs Bess to talk to Raleigh
entities.description: Elizabeth beckons Bess closer and quietly tells her that Raleigh interests her, then commands Bess to go and speak with him, initiating a strategic social maneuver at court.

entities.name: Archduke Charles delivers a nervous compliment to Queen Elizabeth
entities.description: After struggling to compose himself, the shy and trembling Archduke Charles responds to the Queen's remark by declaring that no man could be tired in her presence, offering a formal compliment despite his anxiety.

entities.name: dining hall
entities.description: A generic interior setting where the public meal takes place, inferred from the context of public dining and court attendees present.

entities.name: that night
entities.description: A relative temporal anchor indicating the scene occurs during the evening, consistent with a formal dinner and courtly interactions.

entities.name: Archduke Charles
entities.description: A young nobleman visiting Queen Elizabeth who is nervous and shy in her presence.
entities.summary: A shy sixteen-year-old Austrian nobleman, prompted by his ambassador, delivers a rehearsed marriage proposal to Queen Elizabeth, who declines; he expresses relief and returns home.

entities.name: Bess Throckmorton
entities.description: A lady-in-waiting or attendant to Queen Elizabeth who is directed to interact with Raleigh.
entities.summary: A lady-in-waiting to Queen Elizabeth, involved in personal care and informal interactions, noted for shared smiles and humorous exchanges with the Queen and courtiers like Raleigh and Margaret.

entities.name: Sir Raleigh
entities.description: A court figure who is flirting with court ladies and draws the attention of both Bess and Queen Elizabeth.
entities.summary: A central figure returns to England on a warship, while courtiers vie for the Queen's favor, a petitioner seeks entry, and items like potatoes and tobacco are presented mockingly to the Queen and Don Guerau.

entities.name: court ladies
entities.description: A group of women attending the royal court who interact with Raleigh.

entities.name: imaginary pane of glass
entities.description: A mental construct used by Queen Elizabeth to cope with public dining, visualized as a barrier between herself and others.

entities.name: Elizabeth privately questions Archduke Charles about his true thoughts
entities.description: Elizabeth speaks quietly to Archduke Charles in German, probing whether he ever feels the urge to express his genuine feelings, creating a moment of intimate psychological exchange.

entities.name: Archduke Charles admits he dares not think his true thoughts
entities.description: In response to Elizabeth's probing, Archduke Charles confesses in a hushed tone that he is afraid even to acknowledge his real thoughts, revealing his inner restraint and fear.

entities.name: Elizabeth suggests Archduke Charles would prefer to be at home
entities.description: Elizabeth speculates that Archduke Charles would rather be in his homeland, deepening their private exchange and demonstrating her perceptiveness.

entities.name: Archduke Charles expresses gratitude for Elizabeth's wisdom
entities.description: Archduke Charles acknowledges Elizabeth's insight by calling her wise, and his expression reveals genuine appreciation and emotional connection.

entities.name: Court lady requests a native as a fashion accessory from Raleigh
entities.description: A court lady tells Raleigh she adores the natives he brought back and jokingly asks if she can have one to follow her while dressed in silk, revealing the court's superficiality.

entities.name: Raleigh responds ambiguously to court lady's request
entities.description: Raleigh replies that the danger of the natives depends on what they are used for, subtly criticizing the court's objectification of people.

entities.name: Bess approaches and teases Raleigh about court vanities
entities.description: Bess engages Raleigh, suggesting he might be bored by the superficiality of court life, initiating a deeper conversation between them.

entities.name: Bess draws Raleigh away from the court ladies
entities.description: Bess leads Raleigh physically and conversationally away from the group of court ladies, shifting the focus to a more personal and meaningful exchange.

entities.name: Raleigh compliments Bess by calling her the brightest light
entities.description: When Bess invites Raleigh to leave the court's dazzle, he responds poetically that he is drawn away by the brightest light of all—implying her.

entities.name: Bess and Raleigh observe the Queen watching them
entities.description: Both Bess and Raleigh turn their attention to Queen Elizabeth, who is visibly observing Raleigh, creating a moment of shared awareness and tension.

entities.name: Raleigh bows to the Queen under her gaze
entities.description: Noticing the Queen's attention, Raleigh performs a respectful bow, acknowledging her presence and status.

entities.name: Bess accuses Raleigh of presuming to catch the Queen's eye
entities.description: Bess notes that Raleigh has, in fact, looked toward the Queen despite claiming not to, teasing him about his ambitions.

entities.name: Raleigh claims every man desires money, fame, and love
entities.description: When asked what he truly wants, Raleigh lists money, fame, and love as universal male ambitions, explaining them as interconnected goals.

entities.name: Raleigh explains his plan to build a shining city in the New World
entities.description: Raleigh elaborates that his ultimate purpose is to establish a thriving settlement in the New World, which he views as a meaningful legacy.

entities.name: Bess challenges Raleigh on the order of his desires
entities.description: Bess questions whether money truly comes before fame and love in Raleigh's priorities, prompting him to clarify his motivations.

entities.name: Raleigh asks Bess how to win the Queen's favor
entities.description: Raleigh turns the conversation by asking Bess for advice on gaining Queen Elizabeth's approval, revealing his political and personal ambitions.

entities.name: Bess advises Raleigh to speak truthfully to the Queen
entities.description: Bess counsels Raleigh that instead of flattery, he should offer the Queen honest words, suggesting truth is a rare and valuable gift at court.

entities.name: Queen Elizabeth
entities.description: The Queen who engages in subtle, private conversations with court figures, revealing insight into their inner thoughts and emotions.
entities.summary: The Queen of England, a Protestant monarch opposing Philip of Spain, navigates religious tensions and political pressure regarding Mary Stuart, prioritizes just rule over harsh measures, monitors Spanish threats, and asserts her authority amid council debates and public duties.

entities.name: mulberry-coloured silk
entities.description: A specific fabric color mentioned in the context of dressing a native as a fashion accessory, symbolizing courtly excess and exoticism.

entities.name: cloak
entities.description: A garment that a court lady imagines being carried by a native attendant, representing status and vanity.

entities.name: New World Colony
entities.description: A nascent settlement in the Americas that Raleigh plans to develop into a shining city, representing ambition and imperial aspiration.

document_metadata.title: 39、EXT. WINDSOR GREAT PARK - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Elizabeth and Raleigh share a poignant, flirtatious exchange about love and connection, acknowledging deep mutual understanding; they race back to court, with Elizabeth watching him depart, underscoring unspoken affection and emotional restraint.

entities.name: Elizabeth and Raleigh race on horseback through the woodland ride
entities.description: Elizabeth and Raleigh engage in a high-speed horseback race along a forest path, riding neck and neck before Raleigh pulls ahead, their faces alight with exhilaration and laughter.

entities.name: Raleigh pretends his horse bolts forward out of turn
entities.description: After Elizabeth rides past him, Raleigh secretly spurs his horse to surge ahead, then feigns loss of control by reining in the horse and apologizing to Elizabeth, claiming the animal does not yet know its place.

entities.name: Elizabeth challenges Raleigh about love and marriage
entities.description: While riding, Elizabeth questions Raleigh about his unmarried status, leading to a flirtatious exchange about the distinction between love and marriage, revealing mutual attraction and intellectual rapport.

entities.name: Elizabeth asserts her autonomy in love and duty
entities.description: Elizabeth declares that while she will marry for political reasons, her love belongs to herself, drawing a clear boundary between her public role as queen and private emotional life.
